subject: biology
promptStrong: Give me a 6-mark exam-style question on {lo} for {board} {level} {subject}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a worked example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: A piece of potato is placed in pure (distilled) water. What is most likely to happen to its cells?
options: Water leaves the cells and they become flaccid
Water enters the cells by osmosis and they become turgid
Sugar diffuses out of the cells
The cells lose mass
questions.explain: Pure water is more dilute than the cell contents, so water enters by osmosis, making cells turgid and increasing mass.

questions.q: In an osmosis investigation, a potato chip GAINED mass. This shows the solution it was in was:
options: The same concentration as the cell contents
More concentrated than the cell contents
More dilute than the cell contents
Pure salt
questions.explain: Gaining mass means water entered by osmosis, so the surrounding solution was more dilute than the cell contents.

questions.q: Root hair cells are well adapted for absorbing water because they:
options: Carry out active transport of water
Contain many chloroplasts
Have a large surface area and a thin cell wall
Have a thick waxy layer
questions.explain: A large surface area and thin wall maximise water uptake by osmosis (water is never moved by active transport).

Water from a dilute to a more concentrated solution through a partially permeable membrane
Water from a concentrated to a dilute solution
Any dissolved solute across a membrane
questions.explain: Osmosis is the diffusion of water only, from a dilute (high water) to a more concentrated (low water) solution through a partially permeable membrane.

questions.q: A cell placed in a concentrated salt solution loses water and shrinks. This is because water moves:
options: Out of the cell by active transport
Into the cell by diffusion of salt
Into the cell by osmosis
Out of the cell by osmosis down its water gradient
questions.explain: The salt solution has a lower water concentration, so water leaves the cell by osmosis.

questions.q: Which change would INCREASE the rate of diffusion?
options: A smaller surface area
A higher temperature
A smaller concentration gradient
A longer diffusion distance
questions.explain: Higher temperature gives particles more kinetic energy, increasing diffusion rate; larger surface area, steeper gradient and shorter distance also help.

questions.q: Which of these is a passive process (needs no energy from respiration)?
options: Active transport of glucose in the gut
Osmosis
Uptake of mineral ions by roots
Reabsorption of glucose in the kidney
questions.explain: Osmosis (and diffusion) are passive; active transport requires energy.

questions.q: Diffusion is best described as the movement of particles:
options: Against a concentration gradient
Of water only across a membrane
From a low to a high concentration using energy
From a high to a low concentration down a concentration gradient
questions.explain: Diffusion is the net movement of particles from high to low concentration, down the gradient, and is passive.

questions.q: Water moves into a cell by osmosis when the cell is surrounded by a solution with:
options: No water molecules
A lower water concentration than the cell
A higher water concentration than the cell
The same water concentration as the cell
questions.explain: Water moves from where there is more water (more dilute solution) into the cell.

questions.q: As an organism gets larger, its surface area to volume ratio:
options: Doubles
Decreases
Stays the same
Increases
questions.explain: Larger organisms have a smaller surface area to volume ratio, so they need specialised exchange surfaces and transport systems.

questions.q: Plant roots absorb mineral ions from very dilute soil solutions by active transport because:
options: The ions must be moved against the concentration gradient into the root
Osmosis pulls the ions in
The ions move down their concentration gradient
The ion concentration is higher in the soil than in the root
questions.explain: Mineral ions are usually more concentrated inside the root, so they must be moved against the gradient by active transport.

questions.q: Active transport differs from diffusion because it:
options: Requires energy from respiration to move substances against the gradient
Moves substances down the concentration gradient
Only moves water molecules
Does not require a cell membrane
questions.explain: Active transport moves substances against the concentration gradient and needs energy (ATP) from respiration.
